name: System Network Configuration Discovery
text: T1422 System Network Configuration Discovery: adversary code queries connectivity and Wi-Fi APIs (ConnectivityManager, WifiManager on Android) to learn network configuration such as SSID, IP address, and transport type — typically as a reconnaissance step early in an attack chain, before further action is taken.

name: Compromise Software Supply Chain
text: T1474.003 Compromise Software Supply Chain: a malicious payload is bundled inside an otherwise benign-looking application (e.g. a utility or flashlight app) and distributed via sideloading or an unofficial channel, so the victim installs the malicious functionality unknowingly under cover of legitimate-seeming functionality.

name: Scheduled Task/Job
text: T1603 Scheduled Task/Job: adversary code registers a periodic background job (WorkManager, AlarmManager, or JobScheduler on Android) so that malicious functionality re-executes independently of the app being in the foreground, providing persistence across reboots and app backgrounding.

name: Encrypted Channel
text: T1521 Encrypted Channel: adversary code establishes a TLS-encrypted socket connection to a command-and-control (C2) server to conceal the content of outbound communications from network inspection, often beaconing device information shortly after connecting.

name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
text: T1646 Exfiltration Over C2 Channel: adversary code reuses an existing command-and-control channel to transmit collected or targeted data off the device, rather than opening a separate exfiltration channel — commonly observed immediately following a C2 beacon on the same encrypted socket.

name: Foreground Persistence
text: T1541 Foreground Persistence: adversary code starts a foreground service with a low-priority, benign-looking notification to keep the app process alive and resistant to backgrounding or task-kill by the OS, extending the window during which other malicious behavior can execute.
